_doc: The combined likelihood. Read by mf/trexcfg.adapt_channel; every entry is explained in README.md.
observable: sigma(pp -> Z/gamma* -> ll), 60 < m_ll(LHE) < 120 GeV, sqrt(s) = 13 TeV, per lepton flavour, lepton universality

poi.name: mu_Z
poi.title: #mu_{Z}
poi.reference_note: aMC@NLO (NNLO-normalised) sigma(60 < m_LHE(mumu) < 120) of z-mumu; sigma = mu_Z x reference_pb

ee.label: ee
ee.sigma_reference_source: z-ee/Zee_fit.tar.gz: Zee_fit/reference_cross_section.txt (6077.22 pb x sum w(LHE ee, 60-120) / sum w)
ee.acceptance_note: none outside the fit: the DYee template is normalised to the 60-120 GeV LHE cross section and its PDF / QCDScale / PS_FSR templates carry the extrapolation
ee.split_shape_norm_note: every HISTO systematic of ee enters twice: its normalisation keeps the shared name (correlated with mumu/tautau), its shape gets an ee-only parameter <NP>_eeShape. Without it the ee peak shape (6.3M events in 2 GeV bins, saturated-model p = 7e-43) pins the +-5.9% ElectronID normalisation at 0.08 sigma and drags Pileup/L1Prefiring/QCDScale into mumu; the fully correlated three-channel fit then has no positive-definite minimum. See README.md, 'The ee channel'.

tautau.label: #tau_{h}#tau_{h}
tautau.drop_empty_bins_note: 0 < m_tt < 40 GeV of the BDT > 0.90 category: 0 data events and 0 predicted events. It carries no information, but its MC-statistics gamma is unconstrained and sits at 0, which breaks HESSE/MINOS and makes the per-bin offset log(0)

fit._doc: extra Fit/MultiFit options for every likelihood. Deliberately empty: NLLOffset 'bin' would help the precision of the 2M-event bins but ROOT 6.40 returns NaN for bins with zero observed events (RooFit::Detail::MathFuncs::nll, 0 x log 0), which tautau has; the default 'initial' offset converges once the empty tautau bin is dropped and the ee shape is split off.

variations._doc: Alternative likelihoods, each fitted with the common POI only (run.py variations). 'channels' restricts the fit; 'split' overrides split_shape_norm per channel; 'overall' replaces the normalisation part of a split systematic by a symmetric OVERALL of that size.

ee_electron_id_1p2.label: ee: ElectronID norm. #pm1.2%
ee_electron_id_1p2.note: diagnostic: the UL2016postVFP Medium-ID SF map (datasets/corrections, POG/EGM) gives +-0.3-1.6% per electron outside the ECAL gap, 1.2% per Z->ee event; inside 1.444 < |eta_SC| < 1.566, which z-ee does not veto, it is sf = 1 +- 1. Not a result: it uses a number z-ee did not deliver.
